policy: waves by dependency depth; within a wave tier asc then name; canary services always wave 0 (deps assumed already live)
bug_report: The rollout order for yesterday's release looked random - a dependent service went out before the thing it reads from, and the checkout blip during release is back. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix plan_waves so a service never rolls out ahead of what it depends on, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: stage plan_waves rollouts by dependency depth, tier, and the canary wave
decision_rationale: A release started checkout's API before the cache it reads from had gone out, which caused the serving blip during rollout. plan_waves now levels services into waves by dependency depth - a service deploys in the wave AFTER the deepest of its dependencies. Within a wave the most critical services go first: tier ascending (tier 0 first), then name A-Z so the plan is deterministic. Services marked canary form wave 0 and always deploy first regardless of their dependencies - ops decision: canaries validate the release before anything else rolls, and their dependencies are assumed already live from the previous release; the canary wave is ordered by name, and with no canaries there is no empty leading wave.
